events.label: A smaller working reach leaves a wider sort of day
events.description: From late 2023 Nora accepts fewer overhead installations, shares some fabrication jobs and uses a supported work surface. Income and autonomy both shrink; time for writing becomes less furtive. Owen agrees to protect one morning if Nora also protects his weekend company with friends. She is adapting, not cured or freed from material needs.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: The shoulder will not accept a more accurate plan
events.description: In 2023 recurring shoulder pain makes overhead fitting unreliable. Nora initially moves heavy work to the end of the day so colleagues will not see her slow down. After dropping a tool without injury she tells a collaborator and changes the jobs she accepts. Medical cause and treatment remain outside this authored account; the relevant change is work capaci…
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: A care rota becomes proof of being a good daughter
events.description: Mabel returns home with partial loss of mobility. Nora and Ben arrange help; Nora keeps records of visits and food. Her copy grows more detailed as paid work becomes harder to fit. She begins to regard an unfilled square as something she must fill and an objection from Mabel as ingratitude. That is Nora’s interpretation, not a verdict on Mabel.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: A shared rota becomes smaller and less flattering
events.description: Over six months Nora asks Mabel which help she wants, asks Ben what he will actually do and accepts paid help for a task she had claimed to manage. Mabel sometimes chooses an inconvenient time and Nora sometimes says no. There is less proof of Nora’s indispensability. She begins staying after a practical task without finding another to perform, though under…
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Nora assumes the practical answer will be hers
events.description: During Mabel’s first hospital week after a fictional stroke, Nora asks about rails, medication delivery and transport before asking her mother what arrangements she wants. Her competence is useful to discharge planning, but she hears requests for rest as details she can schedule.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: The price is paid after the column closes
events.description: By 2014 Nora regularly checks the next day’s rota late at night. She leaves choir early or misses it, becomes impatient with Kit’s stories and redoes Ben’s arrangements without telling him. No new diagnostic label is asserted. Fatigue and the threat to her self-image amplify her existing habit.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: The planned visit is the wrong visit
events.description: In June 2016 Nora arrives during a visit Mabel has arranged with a neighbor and begins discussing the next week across them. Mabel asks her to put away the folder and stay for tea, or come back later. Ben says Nora changed his visit without asking. Nora initially recites what she has done. Nobody disputes the entries; they dispute her right to decide the wh…
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Singing where she cannot be indispensable
events.description: Jo invites her to a small amateur singing group. Nora cannot reliably enter alone and initially practices to remove the embarrassment. On group nights other voices carry the line she drops. She enjoys their terrible rehearsal biscuits, musical teasing and the journey home; the value is not reducible to improving performance or serving the family.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: She returns before she is ready to sing well
events.description: Jo saves her a place without making Nora explain every absence. Nora returns while still tired and enters late in a phrase. The group continues. She starts going for the evening itself and will sometimes leave an unimportant household task until tomorrow. This small permission does not solve the care conflict.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: The workshop closes despite the finished orders
events.description: The fictional employer closes in October 2010 after losing repeat commissions. Nora has completed every assigned handover. Her work was competent and still could not secure the job. She takes commercial display repairs she once considered dull; pride, household costs and grief for the workshop coexist.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Promised commissions thin out
events.description: From spring 2010 Nora sees workshop jobs postponed, then helps pack equipment between commissions. She expects that being the reliable finisher will protect her position and accepts unpaid organizing work without asking what it secures.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: A new author is chosen for continued composition
events.description: Nora is an invented continuing compositional persona for The Book of Conditions, introduced on 27 September 2026. The existing twelve chapters and U01–U17 remain the prior artifact; this life offers a voice and a source of questions for subsequent revision. It is not the recovered biography of whoever wrote those chapters, and the historical narrator is not…
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: The competent observer gets the last word
events.description: Nora begins short fiction in 2008 after Kit sleeps. In her early pieces a capable woman spots an error and delivers a final sentence that explains everyone. Her reading group enjoys the clarity but one member says the people seem to exist to be corrected. Nora dismisses the comment before noticing she has made three endings perform the same maneuver.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: A packed case does not fit its doorway
events.description: Nora draws and helps build a display case in 2001. She has checked the case and transport dimensions but not the last doorway. Her supervisor Sal asks her to telephone the venue before redrawing the plan. Nora first prepares an explanation of why the drawing was right. She finally calls, admits the omitted measurement and helps dismantle the case. The clien…
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Making smaller promises under insecure income
events.description: Through 2011–2013 Nora builds a freelance practice, borrowing bench time and pricing preparation. She sometimes bids too low to look capable, then compensates at home with unannounced evenings. Owen insists that agreeing with a customer is not agreeing for both of them. An invoice book helps with money; their conversation remains harder.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Nora’s attributed inner life
events.description: Her beliefs, attentional strategies, self-image and questions are attributed fiction, not the objective truth of her family or colleagues. Ordinary experiences can expose disagreements between her self-account and her conduct.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: A household loses its assumed spare pair of hands
events.description: Kit’s birth in 2007 exposes how often Nora treats Owen’s time between cooking shifts as slack. They move from favors requested after a job is accepted to a weekly conversation before either takes more work. Neither schedule becomes reliable. Their affection survives irritation; Owen likes cooking for friends and does not exist simply to feed the writer.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Her son asks for a lift, not a life design
events.description: In August 2026 Kit prepares to move away for a course. Nora sends a detailed plan of costs, transport and alternatives before he has chosen a room. He replies asking whether she can help carry boxes. She recognizes the old habit and asks what he wants her opinion on. She keeps her unsent second spreadsheet; insight has not erased anxiety.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: From a correct drawing to an installation someone else can do
events.description: Across the next three jobs Nora includes the delivery route and packing sequence in handover. Sal returns one unnecessarily elaborate checklist. Her competence grows by selecting consequential detail, not by writing down everything. She enjoys seeing a junior fitter succeed without needing her in the room.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Limits that can be spoken
events.description: A quarrel with Mabel and Ben forces her to distinguish documenting a need from deciding for another adult. She begins asking for actual commitments instead of filling empty boxes with her own hours. The change is partial: she still produces immaculate emails before difficult calls. Fiction and singing continue through small failures and pleasures.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Childhood: useful hands and ridiculous theatres
events.description: Nora grows up with her mother Mabel, a school kitchen worker, and brother Ben. During uneven household work schedules, she learns to make herself useful before asking for attention. She builds miniature theatres from cereal boxes, enjoys absurd entrances and insists on keeping the curtain she made even when it catches. This play is not merely rehearsal for …
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Lost work, more care, less listening
events.description: Her small employer loses recurring exhibition contracts and closes. Freelance display and shop-fitting jobs restore income unevenly. After Mabel’s stroke in 2013, Nora organizes care with Ben. Her detailed rota averts missed visits but becomes a way to overrule preferences and avoid saying she is exhausted.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Making a household and beginning to write
events.description: She begins living with Owen, a cook with his own changing shifts; their son Kit is born in 2007. Paid work, childcare and late-night story fragments compete. She joins Jo’s informal singing group and is relieved to be neither leader nor best singer. She sometimes treats Owen’s unscheduled time as available to absorb her deadlines.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Learning to build for other people
events.description: A technical illustration course leads to exhibition fabrication rather than a degree in engineering. Nora learns fitting, lettering, packing and the difference between a drawing and its assembly. A mentor shows her how to declare a mistake before solving it. She is proud of being trusted and privately ashamed of needing instruction.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Leaving room in the present
events.description: A recurring shoulder problem changes how she accepts fabrication work; Kit prepares to leave home. Nora mistakes some requests for advice as requests for design. She negotiates smaller jobs and writing time with Owen, and starts leaving some family questions unanswered. On 27 September 2026 she is selected as the fictional author persona for the Book’s cont…
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Body, fatigue and working reach
events.description: Her physical confidence in the workshop gives way to caring fatigue and later a recurring shoulder limit. Adaptation changes tools, accepted jobs and the rhythm of attention; a clear explanation does not restore energy.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Family and shared care
events.description: A child who earns attention by helping becomes a partner and parent, then an organizing daughter, and later has to share decisions she cannot settle. Other people’s wishes are not evidence of her failure.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Self-image and ways of meeting uncertainty
events.description: She first equates usefulness with being wanted, then a complete record with honesty, and gradually recognizes direct conversation, experiment and unproductive company as different goods. The old defensive strategy returns under fatigue.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Play, friendship and singing
events.description: Model theatres, an undistinguished alto voice, jokes with Jo and unproductive afternoons continue beside duties. Shared pleasure repeatedly escapes the accounting that explains much of her work.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Making and paid work
events.description: Work changes from supervised fitting to trusted delivery, insecure freelance commissions and smaller physically sustainable jobs. Her acquired standards help her notice hidden labor but also make her intolerant of work that will not close neatly.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Writing, attention and revision
events.description: Short fiction begins in fragments after Kit sleeps. Early stories reward the competent observer with the last word; later stories let another person remain difficult. Paid work still competes with writing. The Book is a new continuation project in 2026.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Make every need visible before asking for help
events.description: The rota seems a way to love Mabel without failing at work. Nora allocates most deliberate effort to a defensible plan, some to asking others, and little to trying arrangements she cannot control. This is an authored initial state, not a measured care workload.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Ask whose arrangement this is
events.description: Six months later she spends more deliberate attention asking and negotiating, with small experiments in shared arrangements. Keeping a record remains useful. No permanent conversion or general prediction is claimed.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Recite the record when belonging feels threatened
events.description: During the quarrel she first defends the record, then notices that neither Mabel nor Ben disputes its accuracy. Threat to being needed makes direct conversation hard. The low experiment share denotes what she is considering at this moment, not an inability to change.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Write with accountable limits and room for life
events.description: At the newly chosen composition boundary she deliberately balances supporting claims, listening to the characters she has modeled and trying passages that may discover a new question. Other purposes and uncertainty retain a remainder. These are revisable invented shares, not a voice quality rating.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Protect the correctness of the drawing
events.description: Her first response to the missed doorway is to defend the accurate drawing. She spends little deliberate attention asking what the venue now needs. The later call changes action within this episode; this Cut samples the initial response.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: An old protective plan returns in a new relationship
events.description: Faced with Kit leaving, she again works out a complete plan before talking. She later changes course after his reply, but the first response matters: the learning is context-sensitive rather than an upward moral score.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Say the limit before solving it
events.description: The supplier delay invites a defensive account but Nora now calls first, offers imperfect alternatives and lets the organizer help decide. The sample records deliberate response organization, not the probability of a decision.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: A narrow year still contains irrelevant pleasures
events.description: In a personally quiet period during 2021–2022, Nora and Jo exchange recordings of badly attempted songs and argue about endings in detective novels. Nora grows tomatoes badly on a small paved yard and keeps one plant mostly for its smell. These activities neither conceal a trauma nor carry a required moral; they occupy ordinary life alongside insecure work.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: A jammed cardboard curtain remains part of the performance
events.description: At nine Nora refuses to replace a crooked curtain track in the theatre she and Ben have made. Ben gives the arriving cardboard king a speech about the delay. Nora is initially angry and then laughs hard enough to miss her next cue. Both repair and an unplanned performance can be worthwhile; the later author will be tempted to forget the second.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: A missed fitting is reported before a rescue plan exists
events.description: In March 2018 a supplier delays a mount for a local exhibition. Nora is tempted to wait until she can offer an elegant substitute. She calls the organizer that morning with the limit and two imperfect options. The opening uses a provisional support with an explicit empty space. She loses some fee and the relationship continues. The adaptation costs money an…
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: Nora’s contemporary fictional world, 1978–2026
events.description: An invented contemporary setting sharing calendar labels and place names with Britain, separate from the alternate nineteenth-century world of The Book of Conditions. No event here documents a real person or organization. Commissioned exhibition work, household care, paid time and friendship continue beyond the composition task. The past is authored retrosp…
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.label: The person who refuses the explanation remains in the story
events.description: Between 2018 and 2022 Nora revises short fiction so that an action, an interruption or another person’s refusal can outlast the narrator’s explanation. A fictional local magazine takes two stories; others are declined. She is still pleased when readers call her precise and disappointed when they remember a joke she thought incidental.
events.region: Leeds, in the invented contemporary world

events.description: Nora Vale is a wholly invented woman born in Leeds in 1978. Fabricating exhibition displays taught her to see the labor and imperfect fit behind finished surfaces.
